answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each claimed agent to a Wesolowski VDF: producing its proof requires a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each result needed before the next. GPUs may process separate trials, but cannot parallelize one chain across them or shorten its delay; simulating many clones therefore multiplies sequential work. This strict physical time bottleneck makes Sybil identities costly, creating a grove of checks across every ledge and karst path.
